Daily Brief

The most consequential development today is President Trump's decision to waive congressionally-mandated sanctions on Russia, drawing sharp criticism from US lawmakers and Ukrainian President Zelensky, who addressed an EU summit seeking continued European support [BBC], [France 24], [The Hindu]. The move comes amid deteriorating US-Ukraine relations following a controversial diesel import deal with Moscow. Meanwhile, Yemen's conflict has intensified as Houthi forces struck Aden's presidential palace and airport, killing five and prompting Saudi coalition intercepts of additional missiles targeting oil infrastructure [France 24], [Al Jazeera], [Financial Times]. In France, tens of thousands are expected to demonstrate as students, trade unions, and Yellow Vest remnants unite against rising costs and deteriorating public services, with police already making arrests and deploying tear gas in Paris, Marseille, and Lyon [France 24], [RFI]. The IMF's annual meetings concluded in Bangkok with Managing Director Georgieva warning that low-income nations face mounting debt pressures, spending up to 14% of revenues on repayments amid war spillovers and inflation [Al Jazeera], [Nikkei Asia]. A controversial hepatitis B vaccine trial in Guinea-Bissau, championed by HHS Secretary RFK Jr., faces uncertainty after the country's health ministry denied authorizing the study [The Guardian].

Top Stories
01 Geopolitics

Trump Waives Russia Sanctions Two Days Before Implementation, Sparking Congressional Backlash

  • President Trump signed an executive order Friday waiving sweeping sanctions on Russia's energy sector, financial institutions, and senior officials including Putin, which Congress had passed and Trump himself signed into law in September
  • The Lindsey Graham Act would have authorized tariffs up to 100% on imports from top Russian oil and gas purchasers including China and India, and targeted Russia's 'shadow fleet' of sanction-evading vessels
  • Ukrainian President Zelensky said the US had decided to 'completely disregard' the sanctions; Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev called it 'a historic moment'
  • The waiver follows a US-Russia diesel import deal and restrictions on Ukraine's battlefield satellite network access, with Trump calling Zelensky 'more difficult to deal with' than Putin

02 Conflict

Houthi Missile Strikes Hit Yemen's Aden Palace and Airport as Regional Conflict Escalates

  • Five missiles struck the Al-Maashiq Presidential Palace in Aden on Thursday, killing five people including two of Prime Minister Shaya al-Zindani's bodyguards and wounding 16
  • Two missiles landed on Aden International Airport grounds Friday while a Yemenia Airways flight prepared for takeoff to Cairo; no casualties reported
  • Saudi-led coalition intercepted a ballistic missile headed for Yanbu, a key Saudi oil export hub, plus two cruise missiles over the Red Sea and three drones in Saudi territory
  • Iran denied Saudi accusations of involvement while Houthis claimed they targeted Saudi military headquarters and weapons depots; FT reports Houthis now encircling Taiz, one of Yemen's largest cities

Mass Protests Sweep France as Students, Unions, and Yellow Vests Unite Against Rising Costs

  • French authorities expect 70,000-140,000 demonstrators nationwide as high school students, trade unions, and Yellow Vest activists join forces over cost of living and deteriorating school conditions
  • Police used tear gas and batons in Paris, Marseille, and Lyon as protesters staged unsanctioned marches and erected impromptu barricades; 40 arrested in Paris by 9:30am

04 Policy

Guinea-Bissau Denies Approving Controversial Vaccine Trial Backed by RFK Jr.

  • Guinea-Bissau's Health Minister Quinhin Nantote said the ministry never authorized a hepatitis B vaccine trial that would withhold shots from some newborns, contradicting claims that influenced a Danish ethics committee vote
  • The trial, championed by HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., would enroll 14,000 infants and withhold hepatitis B vaccines from half for six weeks to study 'nonspecific' health outcomes
  • Kennedy praised the research at an anti-vaccine conference, with critics saying he 'wants to make it so we don't use a birth dose here in this country' but cannot conduct such trials in the US due to ethical concerns
  • Danish researchers at University of Southern Denmark had received approval from their home institution's ethics committee based partly on reported Guinea-Bissau authorization
Coverage
The GuardianTwo articles: first reported ethics committee approval citing Guinea-Bissau authorization; second reported ministry denial and characterized Kennedy's approach critically
05 Economics

IMF Warns Low-Income Nations Face Mounting Debt Crisis Amid War Spillovers

  • IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said low-income countries now spend 8-14% of revenues on debt repayments, up significantly from previous years due to higher global interest rates
  • Georgieva stated vulnerable nations are missing out on the AI investment boom driving growth in richer countries while simultaneously facing higher borrowing costs
  • Saudi Finance Minister Mohammed Al-Jadaan noted the Middle East crisis has exposed a divide between Gulf states prepared to withstand turmoil and more vulnerable regional economies needing support
  • The IMF's annual meetings in Bangkok concluded with Georgieva citing both 'optimism and worry' about global economic resilience, AI promises, and risks from inflation, debt, wars, and climate
